messages:
anya: Heads-up — I ran a small experiment this morning to change the preseed mix we use during deploy/autoscale handoff. Wanted to share results and get takes.

sam: nice — can you summarize the change?

anya: TL;DR: instead of a 100% synthetic uniform prefix probe we switched to a 70/30 real-prefix + synthetic mix, where real-prefixes are sampled from the top-500 active prefixes in the last 6h. The synthetic portion is still randomized short completions to exercise batching.

lee: why the change? we were seeing low KV hit-rate on new deploys?

anya: yes. Deploy-time warmers were getting great hit-rate for a small set of hot keys, but a lot of long-tail prefixes were never primed -> cold misses once traffic ramped. That plus autoscale surge made latency tail jump ~30-50ms for first 10k reqs after a scale event.

thomas: interesting. what did the hit-rate delta look like? numbers?

anya: baseline (uniform synthetic): median KV hit-rate during 30m post-deploy = 18%. New mix: median = 41%. Peak improvement on top-100 prefixes was marginal (~5%), but long tail (rank 101-1000) improved from 5% -> 36%. Overall token-level cost dropped ~7% in the window.

maria: perf regressions? any unexpected side effects?

anya: one notable regression: per-request P95 latency increased by ~12ms on small-sequence requests when served on our quantized xformer kernel variant. Profiling points to kernel startup overhead for tiny batch sizes — our synthetic probes increased micro-batching in a way that exposed a kernel dispatch path that isn't optimized for B=1, L<16.

sam: can you paste the profiling snippet and the prober config?

anya: sure — profiling (flamegraph excerpt) showed a cold path labeled `quant_kernel_dispatch` bubbling up, plus overhead in `kv_deserialize` for some keys. Prober config we used: 

```
# prober.yaml
mix:
  real_prefix_sample: 0.7
  synthetic_fraction: 0.3
  real_source_window: 6h
  top_k_real: 500
  synthetic_template: "short_prompt_v2"
  rate_qps: 30
  jitter_pct: 20
```

lee: good to see real prefixes included. Did you change cache keying at all? we had dedup rules that canonicalize whitespace which might collapse distinct user intents.

anya: no keying changes in this experiment — only which prefixes we seed. But discovered an edge: our prefix hash uses first-64 bytes of normalized prompt; some long prefixes >64 bytes were truncated to the same prefix bucket after normalization -> colliding seed coverage caused uneven warming. Filed a small fix (PR #4128) to use a rolling siphash of the full normalized prefix for better spread.

thomas: what's the plan to mitigate the quantized kernel path regression? we don't want to roll back because warm-hit improvements are legit.

anya: options discussed: (1) add a micro-batching tweak in the kernel selection heuristic to prefer fp16 kernel for B<=2,L<=16 (benchmarks show fp16 path has lower dispatch overhead), (2) change prober to avoid micro-batches of size 1 by grouping probes into tiny bursts, (3) deploy a short-term A/B where we only enable real-prefix seeding for 10% of deployments.

maria: leaning to fix kernel heuristic + prober tweak. Kernel change needs perf regression guardrails though.

sam: +1. can infra help with staged rollout and canary metrics?

infra-bot: deploy started: deploy/eng-runtime/preseed-mix-experiment v2 -> canary (sha: ab12c3). See: https://ci/release/9876 :rocket:

anya: thanks infra-bot. We'll roll the kernel heuristic in a separate PR and gate with perf tests: small-batch latency microbench + end-to-end deploy warmup sims. Also adding a scheduled job to recompute top-500 real prefixes every 10m instead of 1h to react to traffic shifts.

lee: about scheduled jobs — watch API quota and cost; recomputing top-k every 10m for all regions might be heavy. Maybe run regional top-k with decay and only recompute full top-k hourly, incremental 10m deltas for top-100.

anya: good call. plan: incremental delta job every 10m for top-100, full job hourly for top-500. Rate-limited prober per region with cap 50 qps.

thomas: do we need to distinguish user vs system prefixes for privacy/compliance? pulling top prefixes from real traffic might capture PII if not normalized properly.

anya: we only store normalized prefix hashes and counts (no raw text). Compliance reviewed and ok, but we added an optional opt-out header to exclude prefixes from being sampled.

sam: when do we expect to have kernel heuristic PR + prober tweak live?

anya: kernel PR in 48h (need perf-run), prober tweak + scheduled job today; will monitor a 6h canary window post-roll. I'll post a short follow-up with the perf dashboards and flamegraphs.

maria: thanks — this looks promising. Also, can we add a simple dashboard card showing warm-hit delta and small-batch P95 so we can watch regressions in real time?

anya: yes — adding cards for KV hit-rate (0-60m), token-cost delta, small-seq P95, and kernel-dispatch time.

deploy-bot: canary promoted to prod? waiting on manual approval.

sam: approving after seeing the 1h canary metrics. :thumbsup:

anya: will post results after 6h. short-term takeaways: mixed real+synthetic warmers are much better for long-tail cache coverage; watch for micro-batch kernel dispatch regressions; incremental top-k and grouped synthetic bursts mitigate costs.
